document_control.title: ClassicModels MySQL Metadata for RAG-Based Natural-Language-to-SQL
document_control.purpose: Provide complete schema, semantic, relationship, metric, query-planning, and retrieval metadata so a RAG pipeline can retrieve the right context before generating SQL.
document_control.consistency_statement: The JSON, TXT, DOCX, and PDF deliverables are generated from this same canonical metadata object.
document_control.scope: Read/query metadata only. It does not contain application code or executable SQL examples.

database_overview.business_domain: Fictional retailer of scale models of classic cars and other vehicles.
business_processes_covered: Sales orders and order line items
Employees, reporting hierarchy, and sales offices
database_overview.historical_time_span: Order and payment activity is historical sample data mainly covering 2003 through 2005.
identifier_conventions: Use exact lower-case table names from the schema.
Use exact camelCase column names from the schema.
Identifiers such as productCode, officeCode, postalCode, phone, extension, and checkNumber are text, even when they contain digits.
No table declares AUTO_INCREMENT in the source schema.
database_overview.currency_note: No currency-code column exists. Monetary columns are normally treated as one common currency in the sample database, but the SQL generator must not label the currency unless the application defines it.
major_absences: No tax, shipping fee, return, refund, or coupon table
No inventory movement history or historical stock snapshots
No supplier master table beyond productVendor text

tables.purpose: Stores sales-office location and territory information.
table_notes: Office performance requires joining offices to employees, then usually customers, orders, and orderdetails.
Territory is an office attribute, not a customer attribute.
officeCode is text even though standard values look numeric.

columns.name: officeCode
columns.aggregation_rule: Count distinct for office counts; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact matching unless the user provides only a partial code.

columns.name: city
columns.business_meaning: City where the office is located.
columns.aggregation_rule: Group or count; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use case-insensitive text matching and normalize common city abbreviations only when unambiguous.

columns.name: phone
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact or contains matching; preserve punctuation and country codes.
cautions: Text identifier; never cast to a number for arithmetic.

columns.name: addressLine1
columns.business_meaning: Primary street-address line for the office.
columns.filter_guidance: Use text search for address lookup.

columns.name: addressLine2
columns.business_meaning: Optional secondary office-address line such as suite or floor.
columns.filter_guidance: Use IS NULL semantics for offices without a second address line.
columns.null_meaning: No secondary address line is recorded.

columns.name: state
columns.business_meaning: State, province, prefecture, or comparable administrative area.
columns.aggregation_rule: Group or count; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Do not assume NULL means missing data; many countries do not use this field in the sample.
columns.null_meaning: Administrative subdivision is not recorded or not applicable.

columns.name: country
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact normalized country values from the data; do not silently merge UK and USA-style abbreviations.

columns.name: postalCode
columns.filter_guidance: Treat as text and preserve leading zeros and spaces.
cautions: Never perform numeric ranges unless explicitly requested and semantically valid.

columns.name: territory
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact values. Note that Japan is stored as its own territory label rather than APAC.

tables.purpose: Stores employees, office assignments, job titles, and the management reporting hierarchy.
table_notes: The employee hierarchy is represented by reportsTo and may require repeated self-joins or recursive logic for multiple levels.
Only employees referenced by customers.salesRepEmployeeNumber are customer-facing assigned representatives.
Employee performance is not stored directly; it is derived through assigned customers and their orders.

columns.name: employeeNumber
columns.aggregation_rule: Count distinct for employee counts; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact numeric matching.

columns.name: lastName
columns.filter_guidance: Use case-insensitive text matching; combine with firstName when names may be ambiguous.

columns.name: firstName
columns.filter_guidance: Use case-insensitive text matching; combine with lastName for person lookup.

columns.name: extension
columns.filter_guidance: Treat as text; preserve the leading x.
cautions: Not a numeric measure.

columns.name: email
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact or case-insensitive matching.

columns.name: officeCode
columns.business_meaning: Office to which the employee is assigned.
columns.aggregation_rule: Group or count by office; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Filter by exact officeCode or join to offices for city/country/territory.

columns.name: reportsTo
columns.business_meaning: Employee number of the employee’s manager.
columns.aggregation_rule: Do not sum. Count direct reports by grouping on this column.
columns.filter_guidance: Use NULL to identify the top-level employee.
columns.null_meaning: Employee has no recorded manager; in the standard data this identifies the President.
columns.join_guidance: Self-join to employees.employeeNumber to retrieve manager details.

columns.name: jobTitle
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact stored titles when possible. Preserve the source-data spelling “Sale Manager (EMEA)”.

tables.purpose: Stores customer organizations, contact information, geography, assigned sales representative, and credit limit.
table_notes: Customer organization and customer contact are represented in the same row.
Customer sales and payments require separate joins; avoid multiplying totals by joining orders and payments at detail level in one aggregation.
Some customers are unassigned to a sales representative and can be lost by inner joins.

columns.name: customerNumber
columns.aggregation_rule: Count distinct for customer counts; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact numeric matching.

columns.name: customerName
columns.filter_guidance: Use case-insensitive exact or contains matching; prefer exact match when a full name is provided.

columns.name: contactLastName
columns.business_meaning: Family name of the customer’s primary contact person.
columns.filter_guidance: Combine with contactFirstName for contact-person lookup.

columns.name: contactFirstName
columns.business_meaning: Given name of the customer’s primary contact person.
columns.filter_guidance: Trim whitespace when displaying or comparing because some sample values contain trailing spaces.

columns.name: phone
columns.filter_guidance: Treat as text; punctuation and country-code formats vary.

columns.name: addressLine1
columns.filter_guidance: Use text matching only when needed.

columns.name: addressLine2
columns.filter_guidance: Use IS NULL semantics to find customers without a second line.
columns.null_meaning: No secondary address line is recorded.

columns.name: city
columns.filter_guidance: Use case-insensitive text matching; normalize abbreviations only when unambiguous.

columns.name: state
columns.business_meaning: Customer state, province, or comparable subdivision.
columns.filter_guidance: NULL is common for countries where this field is not used in the sample.
columns.null_meaning: Subdivision is not recorded or not applicable.

columns.name: postalCode
columns.filter_guidance: Treat as text and preserve leading zeros, spaces, and prefixes.
cautions: Never cast to numeric for ordinary filtering.

columns.name: country
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact stored values; trim unexpected trailing spaces when comparing or displaying.

columns.name: salesRepEmployeeNumber
columns.business_meaning: Employee assigned as the customer’s sales representative.
columns.aggregation_rule: Count customers per representative; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use NULL to identify unassigned customers.
columns.null_meaning: Customer has no assigned sales representative.

columns.name: creditLimit
columns.aggregation_rule: May be summed or averaged only when the business question asks about total or average approved credit; otherwise display per customer.
columns.filter_guidance: Use numeric comparisons. Distinguish zero from NULL.
cautions: Credit limit is not customer balance, revenue, payment total, or available credit.

tables.row_grain: One row per customer payment/check transaction.
table_notes: There is no orderNumber in payments, so direct payment-to-order matching is impossible from this schema alone.
When combining customer order totals and payment totals, aggregate each side separately by customer before joining.
A payment may cover multiple orders or account-level balances; do not invent allocation logic.

columns.name: customerNumber
columns.aggregation_rule: Group payment measures by customer; do not sum the identifier.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact customer number or join to customers for names.

columns.name: checkNumber
columns.aggregation_rule: Count or count distinct; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact text matching.
cautions: Not guaranteed to be globally unique without customerNumber because the primary key is composite.

columns.name: paymentDate
columns.business_meaning: Date the payment was received or recorded.
columns.aggregation_rule: Group by year, quarter, month, or date.
columns.filter_guidance: Use this date for cash-receipt timing, not orderDate or shippedDate.

columns.name: amount
columns.aggregation_rule: Additive across payment rows. Sum for total payments; average for average payment size.
columns.filter_guidance: Use numeric comparisons and aggregate after selecting the correct customer/date scope.
cautions: Currency code is not stored.
Payments are not linked to individual orders.

tables.purpose: Stores the seven product categories and their descriptive content.
table_notes: The exact seven categories are Classic Cars, Vintage Cars, Motorcycles, Trucks and Buses, Planes, Ships, and Trains.
Use products for product-level price, vendor, scale, and inventory analysis.

columns.name: productLine
columns.aggregation_rule: Group or count. Do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact category values or safe case-insensitive matching.

columns.name: textDescription
columns.business_meaning: Plain-text description of the product line.
columns.filter_guidance: Use full-text or contains matching only for semantic description questions.

columns.name: htmlDescription
columns.filter_guidance: Normally exclude from analytics unless the user explicitly asks for web/HTML content.
columns.null_meaning: No HTML description is stored in the standard dataset.
cautions: May contain markup rather than clean business text.

columns.name: image
columns.business_meaning: Optional binary image for the product line.
columns.filter_guidance: Do not select by default; retrieve only when binary content is explicitly requested.
columns.null_meaning: No image is stored in the standard dataset.
cautions: Not suitable for ordinary text-to-SQL result display.

tables.purpose: Stores the product catalog, product-line membership, model scale, vendor, description, stock quantity, cost, and list price.
table_notes: Actual quantity sold and sale price are in orderdetails.
Potential unit margin can be estimated as MSRP minus buyPrice; realized unit margin uses priceEach minus buyPrice.
A product with no orderdetails has no recorded sales in the sample period.

columns.name: productCode
columns.aggregation_rule: Count distinct for product counts; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact text matching; preserve underscores and prefixes.

columns.name: productName
columns.business_meaning: Display name of the scale model product.
columns.filter_guidance: Use case-insensitive exact or contains matching; product names may include years and punctuation.

columns.name: productLine
columns.business_meaning: Product category to which the product belongs.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact known product-line values or join to productlines for descriptions.

columns.name: productScale
columns.business_meaning: Scale ratio of the physical model.
columns.aggregation_rule: Group or count; do not sum as text.
columns.filter_guidance: Treat as a categorical string unless explicitly parsed into a denominator.
cautions: Lexicographic ordering is not the same as numeric scale ordering.

columns.name: productVendor
columns.business_meaning: Vendor or manufacturer name stored directly on the product.
columns.filter_guidance: Use case-insensitive text matching.
cautions: There is no separate vendor table or vendor identifier.

columns.name: productDescription
columns.business_meaning: Long text describing product features and characteristics.
columns.filter_guidance: Use contains/full-text semantics for feature searches; avoid returning the entire text unless requested.

columns.name: quantityInStock
columns.business_meaning: Current inventory quantity snapshot for the product.
columns.aggregation_rule: Additive across different products for a current total-unit snapshot, but not across time because no history exists.
columns.filter_guidance: Use numeric thresholds for low-stock or high-stock questions.
cautions: Not historical stock at order date.
No reserved or committed inventory field exists.

columns.name: buyPrice
columns.business_meaning: Unit purchase/cost price of the product.
columns.aggregation_rule: Average or compare across products; multiply by quantities for estimated cost or inventory cost value.
columns.filter_guidance: Use numeric comparisons.
cautions: Static product-level cost, not a historical cost captured on each order line.
Currency code is not stored.

columns.name: MSRP
columns.business_meaning: Manufacturer’s suggested retail/list price per unit.
columns.aggregation_rule: Average or compare across products; multiply by quantities for list-price value.
columns.filter_guidance: Use numeric comparisons and exact capitalization of the column name.
cautions: MSRP is not actual sales revenue; actual unit sale price is orderdetails.priceEach.

tables.purpose: Stores sales-order header information including dates, status, comments, and customer.
table_notes: Order value is not stored in this table; derive it from orderdetails.
Status applies to the whole order, not individual line items.
Cancelled or disputed orders may still have orderdetail rows; include or exclude statuses according to the business question.
Order dates run from 2003-01-06 through 2005-05-31 in the standard dataset.

columns.name: orderNumber
columns.aggregation_rule: Count distinct for order counts; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact numeric matching.

columns.name: orderDate
columns.business_meaning: Date the customer placed the order.
columns.aggregation_rule: Group by year, quarter, month, or day.
columns.filter_guidance: Use this date for sales-order timing and period-based revenue unless the user specifies shipment or payment timing.

columns.name: requiredDate
columns.business_meaning: Requested or required delivery/shipment date for the order.
columns.aggregation_rule: Group by period or use date differences.
columns.filter_guidance: Compare with shippedDate to evaluate timeliness.

columns.name: shippedDate
columns.aggregation_rule: Group by shipment period or use date differences.
columns.filter_guidance: Use NULL to identify orders not yet shipped in the snapshot.
columns.null_meaning: Order has no recorded shipment date, usually because it is not shipped or is in a non-shipped status.

columns.name: status
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact standard values. Do not infer status from dates when status is available.

columns.name: comments
columns.business_meaning: Optional free-text notes about the order.
columns.filter_guidance: Use contains/full-text style matching for issue or keyword searches.

columns.name: customerNumber
columns.aggregation_rule: Group orders by customer; do not sum.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact customer number or join to customers for names/geography.

tables.purpose: Stores the products, quantities, actual unit prices, and line positions for each order.
tables.row_grain: One row per product line item within an order.
table_notes: Line revenue equals quantityOrdered multiplied by priceEach.
The composite primary key means the same product appears at most once per order in the standard schema.
This table is the bridge between orders and products and creates a many-to-many business relationship.
Always join to orders before filtering by order date or status.

columns.name: orderNumber
columns.aggregation_rule: Group line measures by order; do not sum the identifier.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact order number or join to orders.

columns.name: productCode
columns.aggregation_rule: Group line measures by product; do not sum the identifier.
columns.filter_guidance: Use exact text matching or join to products.

columns.name: quantityOrdered
columns.business_meaning: Number of units ordered for this product on this order.
columns.aggregation_rule: Additive across line items when the selected order statuses and date scope are appropriate.
columns.filter_guidance: Use numeric thresholds and aggregate by order, product, customer, date, or category as needed.
cautions: “Units sold” may need cancelled orders excluded depending on business intent.

columns.name: priceEach
columns.business_meaning: Actual unit selling price charged on the order line.
columns.aggregation_rule: Do not sum unit prices by themselves. Use weighted calculations or multiply by quantityOrdered for revenue.
columns.filter_guidance: Use numeric comparisons; compare with products.MSRP for discounts and products.buyPrice for realized margin.
cautions: This is transactional sale price, unlike products.MSRP and products.buyPrice.

columns.name: orderLineNumber
columns.business_meaning: Display or sequence position of the line within the order.
columns.aggregation_rule: Do not sum. May order lines within one order.
columns.filter_guidance: Filter only when the user explicitly asks for a specific line position.
cautions: Not globally unique and not a business measure.

relationships.business_meaning: Each employee works from one office; an office can employ multiple employees.
relationships.avoidance_note: Do not infer customer office directly; reach it through the assigned sales representative.

relationships.cardinality: one manager to zero or many direct reports
relationships.business_meaning: Employees may report to another employee; the top-level employee has NULL reportsTo.
relationships.avoidance_note: Use distinct aliases for employee and manager roles.

relationships.cardinality: one employee to zero or many assigned customers
relationships.business_meaning: A customer may be assigned to one sales representative; some customers are unassigned.
relationships.avoidance_note: Use an outer join when unassigned customers must remain visible.

relationships.cardinality: one customer to zero or many orders
relationships.business_meaning: Each order belongs to one customer; a customer may have no orders.
relationships.avoidance_note: Use an outer join to find customers without orders.

relationships.cardinality: one customer to zero or many payments
relationships.business_meaning: Each payment belongs to one customer; a customer may have no payments.
relationships.avoidance_note: Payments are customer-level and cannot be linked directly to an individual order.

relationships.cardinality: one order to one or many line items
relationships.business_meaning: Each order line belongs to one order.
relationships.avoidance_note: Joining orders to details changes the grain from order to line item; count distinct orders when needed.

relationships.cardinality: one product to zero or many order lines
relationships.business_meaning: Each order line references one product; products may have no recorded sales.
relationships.avoidance_note: Use an outer join from products to find unsold products.

relationships.cardinality: one product line to one or many products
relationships.business_meaning: Each product belongs to one product line.
relationships.avoidance_note: Product-line name is both identifier and display label.

join_path_catalog.result_grain: One row per order before further aggregation.
One row per order line with product-line attributes.
One row per order line attributed to the customer’s assigned representative.
One row per order line attributed through sales representative to office.

join_path_catalog.intent: Customer ordered value versus paid value
keys: Then join the two customer-level aggregates
join_path_catalog.critical_warning: Do not join raw orderdetails and raw payments together before aggregation; that produces many-to-many row multiplication and inflated totals.

join_path_catalog.result_grain: One row per employee with optional manager.

keys: products.productCode = orderdetails.productCode using an outer join from products
join_path_catalog.result_grain: One row per product before grouping or existence filtering.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Extended sales value of one order line.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Include all statuses only when explicitly requested; for realized sales, normally exclude Cancelled and consider treatment of Disputed/On Hold.
cautions: Currency code is not stored.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Total extended value of an order.
metric_catalog.formula_expression: Sum of line_revenue for one orderNumber
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Apply the user’s requested status scope.
cautions: No stored order total exists.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Total value ordered by a customer.
metric_catalog.formula_expression: Sum of line_revenue across the customer’s orders
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Clarify whether cancelled/disputed/on-hold orders should count.
cautions: This is ordered value, not amount paid or recognized accounting revenue.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Total units on selected order lines.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Usually exclude Cancelled when the phrase is units sold; include all when the phrase is units ordered.
cautions: Status is on orders, so join to orders before filtering.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Average actual unit selling price weighted by units.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Use the same status scope in numerator and denominator.
cautions: A simple average of priceEach is not unit-weighted.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Estimated profit using static product buyPrice as unit cost.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Normally exclude Cancelled; make treatment of disputed/on-hold explicit.
cautions: buyPrice is not captured historically per order line, so this is an estimate.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Estimated gross profit as a percentage of sales value.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Use the same status scope for revenue and profit.
cautions: Protect against zero revenue.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Difference between list-price value and actual line revenue.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Apply the user’s requested status scope.
cautions: Negative values indicate priceEach above MSRP.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Percent below MSRP for an order line.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Status usually does not affect the unit calculation but affects included lines.
cautions: Protect against zero MSRP, although standard data uses positive values.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Current units in stock across selected products.
metric_catalog.recommended_date_basis: Current snapshot; no historical date basis
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Not applicable.
cautions: Do not trend over time because only one snapshot exists.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Estimated current inventory value at product buy price.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Not applicable.
cautions: Currency code is not stored.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Estimated current inventory value at MSRP.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Not applicable.
cautions: This is not expected revenue and ignores discounts and sell-through.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Total amount received from customers.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Not applicable to order status.
cautions: Payments are not allocated to specific orders.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Average amount per payment transaction.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Not applicable.
cautions: Different from average paid per customer.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Difference between total ordered value and total payments for a matched scope.
metric_catalog.recommended_date_basis: Use aligned date windows or lifetime scope on both sides
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Order-side status policy must be explicit.
cautions: This is a proxy, not an accounting accounts-receivable balance.
Payment allocation and opening balances are absent.
Aggregate each side separately before joining.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Number of distinct orders.
metric_catalog.recommended_date_basis: orders.orderDate unless another date is requested
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Apply requested status scope.
cautions: After joining orderdetails, never use raw row count for order count.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Average order total.
metric_catalog.formula_expression: Sum of order values ÷ count of distinct orders
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Use a consistent status scope.
cautions: Compute order totals first or use mathematically equivalent grouped logic.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Days from order placement to shipment.
metric_catalog.recommended_date_basis: orders.orderDate or shippedDate depending the user’s wording
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Only rows with a non-null shippedDate.
cautions: Cancelled or unresolved orders may have no shippedDate.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Difference between actual shipment date and required date.
metric_catalog.formula_expression: shippedDate − requiredDate in days; positive is late, zero is on date, negative is early
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Only rows with a non-null shippedDate.
cautions: Define the sign convention clearly in labels.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Share of shipped orders shipped on or before requiredDate.
metric_catalog.formula_expression: Count of shipped orders where shippedDate ≤ requiredDate ÷ count of shipped orders
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Exclude orders without shippedDate from the denominator unless the user defines a broader service-level metric.
cautions: Report denominator definition.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Ordered-value proxy relative to credit limit.
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Order status scope must be explicit.
cautions: Not available credit and not accounting utilization.
Protect against zero or NULL creditLimit.

metric_catalog.business_meaning: Historical units ordered relative to current stock snapshot.
metric_catalog.recommended_date_basis: Orders over selected historical period plus current stock snapshot
metric_catalog.default_status_policy: Usually exclude Cancelled for units sold.
cautions: Not true sell-through because historical opening inventory and replenishments are absent.

query_intent_routing.notes: Join employees only when sales representative details are requested.
Use orderdetails only for products, quantities, or value.
Revenue is derived; it is not stored in orders.
Do not bring in orders unless comparing customer-level aggregates.
This is a proxy, not a precise accounts-receivable balance.
Attribute orders through the customer’s assigned sales representative.
Office is inferred through sales representative assignment.
Use aliases for employee and manager roles.
Only shipped orders have a measurable actual shipment date.
Use existence/anti-join semantics; do not use inner joins.
Use products as the preserving side.
Results are estimates because buyPrice is static product metadata.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Sum of quantityOrdered × priceEach using orders.orderDate.
ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: The user might mean units, payments, shipped revenue, or only completed orders.
The user needs recognized/accounting revenue or a specific status policy.
The user asks which specific order was paid.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Sum of quantityOrdered × priceEach per order.
ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: Taxes, shipping, or discounts outside line prices are expected; those fields do not exist.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Use priceEach for actual sold price, MSRP for list price, and buyPrice for unit cost.
ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: The wording does not indicate which price concept is intended.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Estimated gross profit using priceEach minus current buyPrice.
ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: The user expects operating profit, tax, shipping, or historical cost.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Customer ordered value minus payments as a proxy.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: The user may mean payments, order count, units, or credit limit.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: No universal default; choose only when the user states revenue, units, profit, order count, or margin.
ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: Always when the metric is absent.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Customer geography when discussing customers; office territory when discussing organization or sales offices.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: The user means managers or all employees.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Orders with status In Process or On Hold and/or shippedDate NULL.
ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: The user’s organization uses a different status definition.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: shippedDate greater than requiredDate for shipped orders.
ambiguity_resolution_rules.clarify_when: Unshipped past-due orders should also count.
The user may want MSRP/list value.

ambiguity_resolution_rules.default_interpretation: Use orderDate for sales/order questions and paymentDate for payment questions.

business_rules_and_constraints: Every order belongs to exactly one customer.
Every order line belongs to exactly one order and one product.
Every product belongs to exactly one product line.
Every employee belongs to one office.
A customer may have no assigned sales representative.
An employee may have no manager only at the top of the hierarchy.
A customer may have zero, one, or many orders and payments.
A product may have zero or many order lines.
orderdetails and payments use composite primary keys.
Foreign-key delete/update cascade behavior is not explicitly declared; do not assume cascade operations.
shippedDate and comments can be NULL.
addressLine2, state, postalCode, salesRepEmployeeNumber, and creditLimit may be NULL in customers.
addressLine2 and state may be NULL in offices.
htmlDescription and image are normally NULL in the standard productlines data.
order status values in the standard data are Shipped, In Process, Disputed, Cancelled, Resolved, and On Hold.
productLine values in the standard data are Classic Cars, Vintage Cars, Motorcycles, Trucks and Buses, Planes, Ships, and Trains.
office territory values are NA, EMEA, Japan, and APAC.
orderLineNumber restarts within each order and is not globally unique.
The same product cannot appear twice in the same order under the composite primary key.
Monetary values contain two decimal places but no currency code.
Dates are DATE values with no time-of-day or timezone.
Text collation is case-insensitive in the source definition, but exact stored values should still be preferred for controlled categories.
sql_generation_guardrails: Generate read-only retrieval statements by default unless the user explicitly asks to modify data.
Never invent a table, column, relationship, status, metric, or currency.
Use only exact schema names and correct key relationships.
Select the minimum necessary tables and columns.
Avoid SELECT-all behavior unless the user explicitly requests every column.
Before aggregation, identify the current row grain and the desired output grain.
Use count distinct for order or customer counts after joining to lower-grain tables.
Aggregate order data and payment data separately before comparing them at customer level.
Use actual sale price from orderdetails.priceEach for sales calculations.
Use products.MSRP only for list-price or discount comparisons.
Use products.buyPrice only as a static cost estimate and label profit/margin results as estimated.
Apply date filters to the date that matches the business question: orderDate, shippedDate, requiredDate, or paymentDate.
Make order-status inclusion/exclusion explicit for revenue, units sold, profit, and order counts.
Preserve rows with NULL relationships when the question asks for missing, unassigned, unsold, unpaid, or no-order entities.
Treat text identifiers and postal/phone fields as strings.
Do not link payments directly to orders.
Do not claim historical inventory, returns, refunds, taxes, shipping charges, net income, or exact accounts receivable from this schema.
Use clear business aliases in the result so derived values are understandable.
If a request is ambiguous and materially changes the metric or scope, ask for clarification rather than guessing.
When a safe default is possible, state the selected interpretation in the response metadata or explanation.

rag_retrieval_design.recommended_strategy: Hybrid retrieval using semantic embeddings plus exact keyword/identifier matching. Retrieve table chunks, relationship chunks, and metric/rule chunks together.
rag_retrieval_design.recommended_top_k: Start with 5 to 8 chunks, then rerank for schema relevance and relationship coverage.
chunking_principles: Keep each table definition and its columns in one coherent chunk or a table-summary chunk plus column-detail chunk.
Keep relationship and join-path guidance separate from individual table chunks so multi-table questions retrieve it.
Keep metric definitions in domain groups such as sales, payments, inventory, and fulfillment.
Keep ambiguity and guardrail rules in a dedicated policy chunk.
Include exact table names, column names, aliases, and user synonyms in every relevant chunk.
Attach neighboring chunk identifiers so the retriever can expand context when a query spans multiple entities.

data_quality_and_limitations.impact: Results are for learning/demo use and not current operational data.
Monetary results must not be labeled with a currency unless configured externally.
Exact paid/unpaid status per order cannot be determined.
Gross profit using buyPrice is an estimate based on current/static product cost.
Inventory trends, stock at order date, and replenishment analysis are impossible.
NULL state/postal values may be normal for international addresses, not necessarily errors.
Some values may contain trailing spaces, punctuation variants, or spelling quirks; trim for display and cautious matching.
Keyword searches may miss synonyms and can produce false positives; semantic retrieval can help.
Ordered, sold, shipped, and realized revenue are different concepts; status policy must be explicit.
Office and employee performance reflects customer assignment, not necessarily the person who processed each individual order.
Vendor details beyond the vendor name cannot be queried.
The source uses MySQL utf8/utf8_general_ci; application-level ingestion should preserve text consistently.
